mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES rebounds from a sharp dip, commuting traffic returns and weekday retail visits rise within four weeks. The mechanism is strongest when TRANSIT also stabilizes, because office trips then convert into store visits instead of staying home.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell to -43.3 at t-1w then recovered to -14.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below its last-4-week mean over the next 28 days even though WORKPLACES stays above -20 for at least two consecutive weeks and TRANSIT does not deteriorate further.

mechanism_narrative: A late-week surge in RESIDENTIAL indicates people staying home more, which reduces discretionary shopping trips and pushes RETAIL_REC lower over the next one to two weeks. The signal fails if home-stay rises only because of holiday travel rather than reduced local activity.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises above +10 week-on-week after a week below +10
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL was 12.0 at t-1w and 7.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days despite RESIDENTIAL staying above +10 for at least one full week and no concurrent rebound in transit or workplaces.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT falls below the low-usage threshold, access to shopping districts weakens and retail-and-recreation mobility declines over the following four weeks. The effect is conditional on workplaces not offsetting the transit loss with a strong commuting rebound.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT is below -25 for at least one weekly mean
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT was -33.3 at t-1w before improving to -21.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall below its last-4-week average in the month after any week with TRANSIT below -25, provided WORKPLACES does not rise above -10 in the same period.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained lift in PARKS often signals favorable weather and more out-of-home leisure, which spills into higher retail-and-recreation mobility within two weeks. The relation breaks if the parks increase is isolated and not accompanied by broader activity recovery.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS jumped from -35.0 at t-2w to -14.6 at t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stays flat or falls over the next 14 days after a two-week PARKS improvement of at least 15 points from its prior trough.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM remains depressed while RESIDENTIAL stays elevated, households substitute toward home-centered trips and avoid discretionary shopping, which lowers RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks. This is strongest when both series move in opposite directions for at least two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM stays below -10 while RESIDENTIAL stays above +7
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM was -15.3 at t-2w and -14.3 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week mean despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining below -10 and RESIDENTIAL remaining above +7 for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A one-week recovery in WORKPLACES signals renewed weekday demand that translates into retail footfall with a short lag. The mechanism acts over roughly one week and should be visible even if transit is noisy, as long as office mobility continues to improve.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises by at least 10 points from the prior weekly mean
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rebounded from -43.3 at t-1w to -14.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve within 7 days after any week in which WORKPLACES rises at least 10 points from the previous week.

mechanism_narrative: During a restriction regime, simultaneous weakness in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES suppresses shopping trips more than either series alone, causing RETAIL_REC to move lower over the next four weeks. The effect disappears once both series recover toward baseline.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT and WORKPLACES were both below baseline in all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline over the next 28 days while both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain below baseline for at least three of the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp weekly drop in PARKS after an elevated week is a sign of weather or seasonality turning less favorable, and retail-and-recreation mobility should weaken within two to four weeks. The hypothesis fails if park mobility recovers immediately or if the decline is offset by a strong commuting rebound.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls by more than 15 points week-on-week after being above -20
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS dropped from -14.6 at t-1w to -36.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days after a PARKS drop greater than 15 points unless TRANSIT also improves by at least 10 points in the same window.
